author: reek
body: The decisive line is verify-published. It parses the certificate, slices the tbsCertificate back out with asn1-raw, and checks the REAL signature over those bytes with the key from 10.1. A decoder that is wrong by a single byte -- one off-by-one in a length, one header included where it should not be -- produces a different message, and Ed25519 says False. The vector is therefore a test of the parser and not of itself.

author: reek
body: The negatives are the other half, and they are the half that matters for a parser fed hostile input. Each one is a DER rule that has cost somebody a CVE, and each MUST decode to None.

author: reek
body: Indefinite length. Legal BER, forbidden in DER, and a decoder that takes it can be walked off the end of the structure it thinks it is reading.
